entities.summary: Ron Jeffries is one of the three founders of the Extreme Programming (XP) software development methodology circa 1996, along with Kent Beck and Ward Cunningham. He was from 1996, an XP coach on the Chrysler Comprehensive Compensation System project, which was where XP was invented. He is an author of Extreme Programming Installed, the second book published about XP. He has also written Extreme Programming Adventures in C#. He is one of the 17 original signatories of the Agile Manifesto.In 2018, Jeffries advocated for abandoning what he termed “Dark Agile,” encouraging developers to return to the original values and mindset of Agile.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the co-founders of Extreme Programming (XP), Ron Jeffries played a crucial role in shaping the Agile methodology. His influence can be seen in the widespread adoption of XP and its subsequent impact on software development practices, with many companies adopting Agile principles to improve their development processes.
